The Qur'an's consistent predication of acts to the servant (e.g., "they do," "they earn") establishes, by linguistic convention, the servant's genuine agency.
chapters.translation:
I say: We have already mentioned twenty verses indicating the affirmation of the act (ʿamal) to the servant. And whoever exhausts the search will find much of this in the Qur'an.

The second term: the act (al-fiʿl). God Most High said: {«And whatever good you do, God is knowing of it»} (2:215); {«And every soul will be fully paid what it has done, and He is knowing of what they do»} (39:70); {«And do good»} (22:77); {«And those who are doers of the zakāh»} (23:4); {«They did not do it except a few of them»} (4:66).

The third term: the making (al-ṣunʿ). He said in Sūrat al-Māʾidah: {«Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from their saying of sin and their devouring of illicit gain? Evil indeed is what they were making»} (5:63). And He said in Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt: {«Indeed, prayer forbids indecency and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of God is greater, and God knows what you make»} (29:45).

The fourth term: the earning (al-kasb). God Most High said: {«And every soul will be fully paid what it has earned»} (3:161); {«Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned»} (30:41); {«Every person is pledged for what he has earned»} (52:21); {«Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned»} (74:38); {«Today every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned»} (40:17).

The fifth term: the making/appointing (al-jaʿl). God Most High said: {«They put their fingers in their ears»} (71:7); {«And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Merciful, females»} (43:19); {«And they have made for God partners from the jinn»} (6:100).

The sixth term: the creating (al-khalq). God Most High said: {«So blessed is God, the best of creators»} (23:14). And this entails that others are creators (in a secondary sense), just as one's saying "Zayd is the most virtuous of the virtuous" entails that others are virtuous. And He said, addressing Jesus: {«And when you create from clay the likeness of a bird»} (5:110). And Jesus, peace be upon him, said, narrating of himself: {«I create for you from clay»} (3:49). And He said: {«And you create falsehood»} (29:17). And He said: {«This is nothing but the creation of the ancients»} (26:137).

The seventh term: the origination (al-iḥdāth). God Most High said, narrating of some humans: {«Until I originate for you from it a mention»} (19:46).

The eighth term: the innovation (al-ibdāʿ). God Most High said: {«And monasticism, which they innovated»} (57:27).

When you have known this, we say: The terms used in the language for attributing an act to its agent are none other than what we have mentioned. And all of them have come in the Book of God Most High in attributing the acts of the servants to them. So whoever denies this attribution is striving to belie the Book of God Most High, openly engaging in denial and nullification — and that is pure unbelief.

The answer: This too falls outside the doctrine we have chosen, which is that the conjunction of power (qudrah) with the motive (dāʿī) entails the act, because it is an act from the agent — except that which is such that when it is characterized by power and decisive will, and the obstacles are removed, the act becomes necessary. And the servant is likewise. Thus he is an agent (fāʿil) and a maker (ṣāniʿ). However, since the Creator of that power and that motive is God, Glorified be He, the whole is by God's decree (qaḍāʾ) and destiny (qadar), His creation (takhlīq) and His origination (takwīn). And by this path it becomes clear that all the terms of the Qur'an are used in their original place without any need for denial or innovation. And by this path it becomes clear that what we have chosen is the best of the doctrines and statements in this matter. And God knows best.

The second aspect of their proofs from the Book of God Most High: the command and the prohibition: {«And race toward forgiveness from your Lord»} (3:133); {«Race toward forgiveness from your Lord»} (57:21); {«Answer the caller of God and believe in him»} (46:31); {«Respond to God and to the Messenger»} (3:172); {«O you who believe, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord»} (22:77); {«So believe — it is better for you»} (4:170); {«And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord»} (39:55); {«And turn in repentance to your Lord»} (39:54); {«And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it»} (59:7); {«Obey God and obey the Messenger»} (4:59).

chapters.title_en: The Third Argument of the Mu'tazilites: Verses Indicating the Absence of Impediments to Faith and the Absence of Compulsion to Disbelief
chapters.arabic_text:
وبالجملة : فالأوامر والنواهي الواردة في كتاب الله ، لا حد لها ولا حصر ، ولو لم يكن العبد قادرا على الفعل والترك ، لم يقبل أمره ولا نهيه ، وكيف يجوز في العقل أن  يقال : افعل يا من لا يفعل؟ ولو جاز ذلك ، فلم لا يجوز أن يبعث الأنبياء إلى الجمادات ، وينزل عليهم الكتب ويملأ تلك الكتب من الوعد والوعيد للجمادات؟ وكما أن صريح لفظ القرآن يشهد بأن كل ذلك سفه وعبث ، فكذلك صريح العقل يشهد بأن أمر العبد ونهيه مع أنه لا قدرة له على

الفعل والترك عبث وسفه.

والجواب : إنا بينا في باب الجواب عن شبههم العقلية : إن تكليف ما لا يطاق ، لازم على المعتزلة من اثني عشر وجها ، فلا فائدة في إعادتها في هذا المقام وبالله التوفيق.

الوجه الثالث من استدلالات القوم : الآيات الدالة على أنه لا مانع لهم من الإيمان والطاعة ، ولا مجبر لهم على الكفر والمعصية. ولنذكر من هذا الجنس آيات :

أحدها : قوله تعالى : ( @QUR@03 كيف تكفرون بالله ) (1)؟ قالوا : هذه الآية دالة على أن الكفر من قبل العبد. وبيانه من وجوه : الأول : لو كان تعالى قد خلق الكفر فيهم ، لما جاز أن يقول : ( @QUR@03 كيف تكفرون بالله ) على سبيل التوبيخ ، كما لا يجوز أن يقول : كيف تسودون وتبيضون وتصحون وتسقمون؟ الثاني : إن كان خلقهم أولا للشقاء وللنار ، أو ما أراد بخلقهم إلا الكفر والوقوع في النار فكيف يصح أن يقول موبخا لهم : ( @QUR@02 كيف تكفرون )؟ الثالث : كيف يليق بالحكيم أن يقول : ( @QUR@02 كيف تكفرون ) حال ما يخلق الكفر فيهم؟ الرابع : إنه تعالى إذا قال للكفار : ( @QUR@02 كيف تكفرون ) فهل ذكر هذا الكلام توجيها للحجة على العبد ، وطلبا للجواب منه ، أو ذكره على سبيل الهزل والبعث؟ والثاني لا يقول به مسلم. فبقي الأول : فنقول : لو كان موجد الكفر هو الله تعالى ، لكان للكافر أن يقول :

عندي اثني عشر وجها من وجوه العذر. كل واحد منها مستقل بأن يكون جوابا عن هذا السؤال : فالأول : أنه يقول : يا إله الخلق خلقت الكفر في ، فكيف لا أكون كافرا. مع أني لا أقدر على دفع فعلك؟ الثاني : أردت الكفر ، وأنا لا أقدر على دفع إرادتك. والثالث : علمت الكفر مني وعند المجبرة : أن خلاف المعلوم ممتنع الوقوع. والرابع : أجبرت على  وقوع الكفر عند المجبرة ، خلاف خبر الله ممتنع الوقوع والخامس : إنك خلقت في قدرة لا تصلح إلا للكفر ، ومع حصول تلك القدرة يكون الكفر واجب الحصول. والسادس : إنك خلقت في إرادة جازمة مقتضية لحصول الكفر ، ومع حصول تلك الإرادة يكون الكفر واجب الحصول. وأيضا : فكما حصلت هذه الأسباب الستة في جانب حصول الكفر ، فهي بأسرها مفقودة في جانب الإيمان. مع أنه يمتنع حصول الإيمان إلا عند حصول مجموعها. فثبت : أنه حصل لعدم الإيمان اثني عشر سببا. كل واحد منها مستقل بعدم الإيمان. فكيف يليق بالحكيم أن يقول مع هذه الموانع القاهرة : ( @QUR@05 وما ذا عليهم لو آمنوا ) (2)؟ أو يقول : ( @QUR@03 كيف تكفرون بالله ) (3) اللهم إلا إذا قاله على سبيل الهزل. إلا أن على هذا التقدير يصير القرآن كتاب الهزل والسخرية.

وثانيها : قوله تعالى : ( @QUR@08 وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى ) (1)؟ وهو إنكار بلفظ الاستفهام (2). ومعلوم : أن رجلا لو جلس في موضع ، بحيث لا يمكنه الخروج ، وقال له مولاه : ما منعك عن التصرف في حوائجي ، كان ذلك الكلام عبثا. وأيضا : المجبرة يقولون : إن الختم والطبع والقسوة والغشاوة والوقر والصم والبكم والعمى والسد والإغواء والإضلال والإرانة والصرف والمكر والاستدراج والخداع (3). وكل واحد من هذه الأمور الستة عشر : سببه مستقل بالمنع من الإيمان. فمع قيام هذه الموانع بأسرها كيف يليق بالحكيم أن يقول : ( @QUR@05 وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا؟ ) وأيضا : الأعذار الاثني عشر قائمة ، ومع حصولها ، كيف يليق بالحكيم أن يقول: ( @QUR@05 وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا ).

وثالثها : قوله تعالى لإبليس ( @QUR@04 ما منعك أن تسجد؟ ) (4) وقول موسى عليه السلام لأخيه :

والطبع كقوله تعالى ( وطبع الله على قلوبهم فهم لا يعلمون طبع الله على قلوبهم وسمعهم وأبصارهم ).

والقسوة كقوله عز وجل ( وجعلنا قلوبهم قاسية. ).

والغشاوة كقوله سبحانه ( ختم الله على قلوبهم وعلى سمعهم وعلى أبصارهم غشاوة ).

والوقر كقوله عز وجل ( وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا ). والصم والبكم والعمى كقوله تعالى ( صم بكم عمي فهم لا يرجعون أولئك الذين لعنهم الله فأصمهم وأعمى أبصارهم  ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور ).

والسد كقوله تعالى ( وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون ).

والإغواء كقوله عز وجل ( قال فبما أغويتني ولا ينفعكم نصحي إن أردت أن أنصح لكم إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم ).
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-م-ر (amara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Command; the act of demanding an action with authority; implies the capacity of the one commanded to comply or refuse.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, a command (amr) presupposes the moral agency of the addressee; otherwise, it is nullified as an act of futility (ʿabath).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage requires the commanded to possess power (qudrah) over both act and omission; metaphorical (majāz) usage here would render the divine address absurd.
- Root: ك-ف-ر (kafara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, conceal; disbelief as the veiling of truth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Disbelief (kufr) as a voluntary act of rejection, entailing culpability; its attribution to God would negate the very basis of blame (tawbīkh).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The interrogative form "how" (kayfa) in {«كيف تكفرون بالله»} is literal reproach, not rhetorical concession.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Interrogative of Reproach (Istifhām al-Tawbīkh) — The particle "kayfa" in this construction demands a rational answer from the addressee; if the addressee lacks agency, the question becomes void, akin to asking "how do you become black or white?" (non-volitional states).
chapters.translation:
In sum: the commands and prohibitions contained in the Book of God are without limit or enumeration. And if the servant were not capable of both the act and its omission, then neither the command nor the prohibition addressed to him would be receivable. How could it be rationally permissible to say: "Do!" to one who does not do? And if that were permissible, then why would it not be permissible to send prophets to inanimate objects, and to reveal books to them, and to fill those books with promises and threats directed at inanimate objects? And just as the explicit wording of the Qur'an testifies that all of that would be folly and futility (safah wa-ʿabath), so too does the explicit reason testify that commanding and prohibiting a servant who has no power over act and omission is futility and folly.

The Answer: We have already demonstrated in the chapter on responding to their rational ambiguities that the imposition of what cannot be borne (taklīf mā lā yuṭāq) is entailed upon the Mu'tazilites from twelve aspects. There is no benefit in repeating them in this context. And with God is the granting of success.

The Third Aspect of the People's (Mu'tazilites') Arguments: The verses indicating that there is no impediment (māniʿ) preventing them from faith and obedience, and no compeller (jābir) forcing them upon disbelief and disobedience. Let us mention from this category some verses:

The First of Them: His saying, the Exalted: {«كيف تكفرون بالله»} (How do you disbelieve in God?) [Q. 2:28]. They said: This verse indicates that disbelief proceeds from the servant. Its demonstration is from several aspects:

The First: If the Exalted had created disbelief in them, it would not be permissible for Him to say: {«كيف تكفرون بالله»} by way of reproach (tawbīkh), just as it is not permissible to say: "How do you become black and white, and how do you become healthy and ill?"

The Second: If He had created them initially for wretchedness and the Fire, or if He had not intended by their creation anything but disbelief and falling into the Fire, then how could it be sound for Him to say, reproaching them: {«كيف تكفرون»}?

The Third: How does it befit the Wise (al-Ḥakīm) to say: {«كيف تكفرون»} at the very moment He is creating disbelief in them?

The Fourth: When the Exalted says to the disbelievers: {«كيف تكفرون»}, is this statement a directing of the proof against the servant, and a seeking of an answer from him, or is it mentioned by way of jest and mockery? The second — no Muslim would affirm it. So the first remains. Then we say: If the originator of disbelief were God, the Exalted, then the disbeliever would have the right to say:

"I have twelve aspects of excuse (wajh min wujūh al-ʿudhr). Each one of them is independently sufficient as an answer to this question." So the First: He says: "O God of creation! You created disbelief in me, so how could I not be a disbeliever, given that I have no power to repel Your act?" The Second: "You willed disbelief, and I have no power to repel Your will." The Third: "You knew disbelief from me — and according to the Compulsionists (al-Mujbirah), the contrary of what is known is impossible of occurrence." The Fourth: "You compelled the occurrence of disbelief — and according to the Compulsionists, the contrary of God's report is impossible of occurrence." The Fifth: "You created in me a power (qudrah) that is fit only for disbelief, and with the existence of that power, disbelief becomes necessarily occurring (wājib al-ḥuṣūl)." The Sixth: "You created in me a decisive will (irādah jāzimah) necessitating the occurrence of disbelief, and with the existence of that will, disbelief becomes necessarily occurring."

Moreover: Just as these six causes are realized on the side of the occurrence of disbelief, they are all entirely absent on the side of faith. And faith cannot occur except when the totality of them is realized. So it is established that there have occurred, for the non-occurrence of faith, twelve causes — each one of them independently sufficient for the non-occurrence of faith. So how does it befit the Wise, given these overpowering impediments, to say: {«وما ذا عليهم لو آمنوا»} (And what would it harm them if they believed?) [Q. 4:39]? Or to say: {«كيف تكفرون بالله»}? — Unless He said it by way of jest. Except that on this supposition, the Qur'an would become a book of jest and mockery.

The Second of Them: His saying, the Exalted: {«وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى»} (And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them?) [Q. 17:94]. It is a denial expressed in the form of an interrogative. And it is known that if a man were seated in a place such that he could not exit, and his master said to him: "What prevented you from attending to my needs?" — that speech would be futility. Moreover, the Compulsionists say: The sealing (khatm), the stamping (ṭabʿ), the hardness (qaswah), the covering (ghishāwah), the heaviness (waqr), the deafness (ṣamam), the muteness (bakam), the blindness (ʿamā), the barrier (sadd), the misguidance (ighwā'), the leading astray (iḍlāl), the veiling (irānah), the turning away (ṣarf), the deception (makr), the gradual seduction (istidrāj), and the trickery (khidāʿ) — and each one of these sixteen matters has a cause independently sufficient to prevent faith. So with all of these impediments standing, how does it befit the Wise to say: {«وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا»}? Moreover, the twelve excuses are standing, and with their existence, how does it befit the Wise to say: {«وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا»}?

The Third of Them: His saying, the Exalted, to Iblīs: {«ما منعك أن تسجد»} (What prevented you from prostrating?) [Q. 7:12], and the saying of Moses, peace be upon him, to his brother [Aaron]:

And the stamping (ṭabʿ), as in His saying, the Exalted: {«وطبع الله على قلوبهم فهم لا يعلمون»} (And God stamped upon their hearts, so they do not know) [Q. 9:93] — and {«طبع الله على قلوبهم وسمعهم وأبصارهم»} (God stamped upon their hearts, their hearing, and their sight) [Q. 16:108].

And the hardness (qaswah), as in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: {«وجعلنا قلوبهم قاسية»} (And We made their hearts hard) [Q. 5:13].

And the covering (ghishāwah), as in His saying, the Glorious: {«ختم الله على قلوبهم وعلى سمعهم وعلى أبصارهم غشاوة»} (God sealed their hearts, their hearing, and their sight with a covering) [Q. 2:7].

And the heaviness (waqr), as in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: {«وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا»} (And We placed upon their hearts veils lest they comprehend it, and in their ears heaviness) [Q. 6:25].

And the deafness, muteness, and blindness, as in His saying, the Exalted: {«صم بكم عمي فهم لا يرجعون»} (Deaf, dumb, blind — so they do not return) [Q. 2:18], and {«أولئك الذين لعنهم الله فأصمهم وأعمى أبصارهم»} (Those are the ones whom God cursed, so He deafened them and blinded their sight) [Q. 47:23], and {«ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور»} (But blind are the hearts that are in the breasts) [Q. 22:46].

And the barrier (sadd), as in His saying, the Exalted: {«وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون»} (And We placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We covered them, so they do not see) [Q. 36:9].

And the misguidance (ighwā'), as in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: {«قال فبما أغويتني»} (He said: "Because You have misguided me") [Q. 7:16], and {«ولا ينفعكم نصحي إن أردت أن أنصح لكم إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم»} (And my counsel will not benefit you if I intend to counsel you, if God intends to misguide you) [Q. 11:34].

chapters.title_en: On the Heart's Impediments to Guidance and the Validity of Divine Rebuttal (Al-Mawāniʿ al-Qalbiyyah wa Ithbāt al-Munāẓarah maʿa Allāh)
chapters.arabic_text:
والإضلال كقوله سبحانه ( فمن يهدي من أضل الله الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله أضل أعمالهم وأضله الله على علم قل إن الله يضل من يشاء ) والإرانة من الران قال تعالى ( كلا بل ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون ) والصرف كقوله جل وعلا ( صرف الله قلوبهم بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون ). والمكر كقوله تعالى ( أفأمنوا مكر الله فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون ) والاستدراج كما قال عز وجل ( سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون ) والخداع كقوله سبحانه ( إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم ). قلت ومن الموانع التي لم يذكرها الرازي رحمه الله وهي أيضا مما يتعلق بالقلوب :

القفل قال تعالى ( أم على قلوب أقفالها ).

والأكنة ( وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة ).

الغفلة قال عز وجل ( ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا ).

المرض قال سبحانه ( في قلوبهم مرض فزادهم الله مرضا ).

الزيغ ( فلما زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم ).

عدم الفقه أو العقل ( لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها ).

الريبة : قال تعالى ( وارتابت قلوبهم فهم في ريبهم يترددون ).

اللهو : قال عز وجل ( لاهية قلوبهم ).

الغمرة : قال سبحانه ( بل قلوبهم في غمرة من هذا ).

( @QUR@05 ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا ) (1)؟ وقوله ( @QUR@04 فما لهم لا يؤمنون ) (2)؟ و ( @QUR@05 فما لهم عن التذكرة معرضين ) (3) ( @QUR@06 عفا الله عنك. لم أذنت لهم ) (4) ( @QUR@06 لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك ) (5) ( @QUR@04 لم تلبسون الحق بالباطل ) (6)؟ ( @QUR@05 لم تصدون عن سبيل الله ) (7)؟.

وقال «الصاحب بن عباد» في فصل له في هذا الباب : «كيف يأمر بالإيمان ولم يرده ، وينهي عن الكفر ويريده ، ويعاقب على الباطل ويقدره ، وكيف يصرفه عن الإيمان ، ثم يقول : ( @QUR@02 أنى يصرفون ) (8) ويخلق فيهم الإفك ، ثم يقول : ( @QUR@02 أنى يؤفكون ) (9)؟ وينشأ فيهم الكفر ، ثم يقول : ( @QUR@02 لم تكفرون ) (10)؟ ويخلق فيهم لبس الحق بالباطل ثم يقول : ( @QUR@04 لم تلبسون  الحق بالباطل ) (11) ويصدرهم عن سبيل الله ، ثم يقول : ( @QUR@05 لم تصدون عن سبيل الله ) (12)؟ وحال بينهم وبين الإيمان ، ثم يقول : ( @QUR@05 وما ذا عليهم لو آمنوا ) (13)؟ وذهب بهم عن الرشد ثم قال: ( @QUR@02 فأين تذهبون ) (14) وأضلهم عن الدين ، حتى أعرضوا ، ثم قال : ( @QUR@05 فما لهم عن التذكرة معرضين ) (15).

فإن قال قائل : إن السؤال والجواب إنما يتم مع الأكفاء والأمثال ، والله منزه عن ذلك. فكيف تمكن المناظرة مع الله؟ ولهذا قال تعالى : ( @QUR@04 لا يسئل عما يفعل ) (16).

فالجواب عنه من وجهين :

الأول : إن المناظرة مع الله ، إذا كانت ممتنعة كان إيراد هذا السؤال من الله يجب أن يكون عبثا ، وذلك يقتضي القدح في كلمة الله تعالى.

الثاني : إن القرآن قد دل على أن هذه المناظرة غير ممتنعة. ويدل عليه آيات : أحدها :

قوله تعالى : ( @QUR@024 يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم على فترة من الرسل أن تقولوا : ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير. فقد جاءكم بشير ونذير ) (1) وثانيها : قوله تعالى : ( @QUR@011 رسلا مبشرين ومنذرين. لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل ) (2) وثالثها : قوله تعالى : ( @QUR@020 ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله ، لقالوا : ربنا لو لا أرسلت إلينا رسولا ، فنتبع آياتك من قبل أن نذل ونخزى ) (3) ورابعها : قوله تعالى : ( @QUR@09 أولم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر ، وجاءكم النذير ) (4)؟ ومعلوم أن المراد منه : إنا أمهلناكم وأزلنا عذركم حتى لا يبقى لكم عذر ولا حجة علينا. وخامسها : قوله تعالى : ( @QUR@07 يوم تأتي كل نفس تجادل عن نفسها ) (5) ومعلوم أن تلك المجادلة إنما تكون مع من يطالبها ويجانسها. وما ذاك إلا الله تعالى. فيلزم أن تكون مجادلة العبد مع الله. وسادسها : قوله تعالى حكاية عن الكفار : ( @QUR@07 رب لم حشرتني أعمى. وقد كنت بصيرا ) (6) ؟ ثم لم يقل في الجواب : ( @QUR@04 لا يسئل عما يفعل ) (7) بل قال : ( @QUR@07 كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى ) (8) وسابعها : قوله : ( @QUR@022 وأنفقوا من ما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت ، فيقول : رب لو لا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب : فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين ) (9).
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deviation from the straight path; loss of the way; perishing in error.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, iḍlāl (misguidance) is God's just act of abandoning the obstinate sinner to his own choice, not the coercive creation of unbelief.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical straying; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual deprivation of tawfīq (divine facilitation).
- Root: ر-ي-ن (r-y-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Rust or tarnish covering a surface, obscuring its original brightness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The "stain" (rān) upon the heart is the cumulative effect of sins that veils the faculty of discernment (baṣīrah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical extension from physical rust to moral-spiritual blindness.
- Root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Crafty scheming; devising a plan to harm another while concealing one's intent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): For God, makr is requital (mukāfaʾah) — matching the sinner's deception with a just consequence, not initiating evil.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Majāz when applied to God; the literal sense (deceitful plotting) is impossible for Him.
- Root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Gradual ascent by steps; moving from one stage to another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Istdrāj is God's gradual leading of the sinner toward destruction through successive blessings, so that he becomes engrossed and forgets repentance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical — the "steps" are increments of grace that become a snare.
- Root: خ-د-ع (kh-d-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deception; causing someone to act against his own interest through false hope.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): For God, khudāʿ is the just recompense of the hypocrites' deception — He "deceives" them by granting respite that increases their ruin.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Majāz; the literal sense is impossible for God, so it denotes requital in kind.
- Root: ق-ف-ل (q-f-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A lock; sealing shut a container or door.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The "locks" on hearts signify the final state of hardness after repeated rejection of truth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical for the heart's imperviousness to admonition.
- Root: غ-ف-ل (gh-f-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Neglect; heedlessness; absence of attention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): God's "making heedless" is a punitive consequence of the person's own prior neglect of remembrance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for human inattention; metaphorical for divine abandonment.
- Root: ز-ي-غ (z-y-gh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Swerving; inclining away from the middle course.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Quran, izāghah (causing to swerve) follows the creature's own zaygh (swerving) as a just penalty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical deviation; metaphorical for doctrinal corruption.
- Root: ر-ي-ب (r-y-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Doubt; suspicion; disturbance of certainty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Rayb is the unsettled state of the heart that prevents firm assent (taṣdīq).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for psychological uncertainty.
- Root: غ-م-ر (gh-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deep water that covers; overwhelming flood.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ghimrah is the covering of the heart by heedlessness, like water submerging a swimmer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical for total envelopment in ignorance.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-Istifhām al-Inkārī (Interrogative of Denial/Reproach) — The rhetorical questions in the cited verses (e.g., «فما لهم لا يؤمنون») function as rebuke (tawbīkh), presupposing the addressee's culpability, not as genuine requests for information. This syntactic form is crucial for the theological argument: God's questioning implies the creature's responsibility.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the impediments to guidance which the Imam (al-Rāzī, may God have mercy on him) mentioned in this section are of two kinds: those that pertain to the heart's receptivity, and those that pertain to divine acts of requital. As for the divine acts, they are: misguidance (iḍlāl), as His saying, the Exalted: {«فمن يهدي من أضل الله»} (Then who will guide him whom God has led astray?) [Q 13:33], and His saying: {«الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله أضل أعمالهم»} (Those who disbelieve and bar from the way of God — He has made their works go astray) [Q 47:1], and His saying: {«وأضله الله على علم»} (And God led him astray knowingly) [Q 45:23], and His saying: {«قل إن الله يضل من يشاء»} (Say: Indeed God leads astray whom He wills) [Q 13:27]. And the "staining" (irānah), from al-rān, as He, the Exalted, said: {«كلا بل ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون»} (Nay, but that which they earned has stained their hearts) [Q 83:14]. And the "turning away" (ṣarf), as His saying, Glorious and Exalted: {«صرف الله قلوبهم بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون»} (God has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not understand) [Q 9:127]. And the "scheming" (makr), as His saying, the Exalted: {«أفأمنوا مكر الله فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون»} (Do they then feel secure from God's scheme? None feels secure from God's scheme except the losing folk) [Q 7:99]. And the "gradual leading on" (istidrāj), as He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} (We shall gradually lead them on from whence they know not) [Q 7:182]. And the "deception" (khidāʿ), as His saying, the Exalted: {«إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم»} (The hypocrites seek to deceive God, but He is deceiving them) [Q 4:142].

I say: And among the impediments which al-Rāzī (may God have mercy on him) did not mention — and these too pertain to the hearts — are the following:

The lock (al-qufl), as He, the Exalted, said: {«أم على قلوب أقفالها»} (Or are there locks upon their hearts?) [Q 47:24].

And the coverings (al-akinnah), as He said: {«وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة»} (And We have placed coverings over their hearts) [Q 6:25].

Heedlessness (al-ghaflah), as He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا»} (And do not obey him whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance) [Q 18:28].

Sickness (al-maraḍ), as He said, the Exalted: {«في قلوبهم مرض فزادهم الله مرضا»} (In their hearts is a sickness, and God has increased them in sickness) [Q 2:10].

Deviation (al-zaygh), as He said: {«فلما زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم»} (So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate) [Q 61:5].

Lack of understanding or intellect, as He said: {«لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها»} (They have hearts with which they do not understand) [Q 7:179].

Doubt (al-raybah), as He, the Exalted, said: {«وارتابت قلوبهم فهم في ريبهم يترددون»} (And their hearts were doubtful, so they waver in their doubt) [Q 9:45].

Amusement (al-lahw), as He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«لاهية قلوبهم»} (Their hearts are distracted) [Q 21:3].

The overwhelming flood (al-ghimrah), as He said, the Exalted: {«بل قلوبهم في غمرة من هذا»} (Nay, but their hearts are in a flood of this) [Q 23:63].

Then the author proceeds to cite the divine interrogations that imply the creature's accountability, such as His saying: {«ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا»} (What prevented you, when you saw them go astray?) [Q 20:92], and His saying: {«فما لهم لا يؤمنون»} (So what is the matter with them that they do not believe?) [Q 85:20], and {«فما لهم عن التذكرة معرضين»} (So what is the matter with them that they turn away from the reminder?) [Q 74:49], and {«عفا الله عنك. لم أذنت لهم»} (May God pardon you! Why did you permit them?) [Q 9:43], and {«لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك»} (Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?) [Q 66:1], and {«لم تلبسون الحق بالباطل»} (Why do you clothe the truth with falsehood?) [Q 3:71], and {«لم تصدون عن سبيل الله»} (Why do you bar from the way of God?) [Q 3:99].

And al-Ṣāḥib ibn ʿAbbād said in a chapter of his on this topic: "How can He command faith while not willing it, and forbid unbelief while willing it, and punish falsehood while decreeing it? And how can He turn them away from faith, then say: {«أنى يصرفون»} (How are they turned away?) [Q 9:74]? And He creates in them falsehood, then says: {«أنى يؤفكون»} (How are they deluded?) [Q 9:30]? And He originates unbelief in them, then says: {«لم تكفرون»} (Why do you disbelieve?) [Q 3:98]? And He creates in them the clothing of truth with falsehood, then says: {«لم تلبسون الحق بالباطل»} (Why do you clothe the truth with falsehood?) [Q 3:71]? And He makes them issue forth from the way of God, then says: {«لم تصدون عن سبيل الله»} (Why do you bar from the way of God?) [Q 3:99]? And He interposes between them and faith, then says: {«وما ذا عليهم لو آمنوا»} (And what would it harm them if they believed?) [Q 4:39]? And He takes them away from right guidance, then says: {«فأين تذهبون»} (So where are you going?) [Q 81:26]? And He leads them astray from the religion until they turn away, then says: {«فما لهم عن التذكرة معرضين»} (So what is the matter with them that they turn away from the reminder?) [Q 74:49]."

Now if someone says: "Question and answer are only valid between peers and equals, and God is exalted above that. So how can disputation (munāẓarah) with God be possible? For this reason He, the Exalted, said: {«لا يسئل عما يفعل»} (He is not questioned about what He does) [Q 21:23]."

The answer to this is from two aspects:

The first: If disputation with God were impossible, then God's own posing of such questions would have to be an act of futility (ʿabath), and that would entail an impeachment of the Word of God, the Exalted.

The second: The Quran has indicated that this disputation is not impossible. This is shown by several verses. One of them is His saying, the Exalted: {«يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم على فترة من الرسل أن تقولوا: ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير. فقد جاءكم بشير ونذير»} (O People of the Scripture! There has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you, after an interval between the messengers, lest you say: 'There has not come to us any bearer of good tidings or warner.' But there has come to you a bearer of good tidings and a warner) [Q 5:19]. The second is His saying, the Exalted: {«رسلا مبشرين ومنذرين. لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل»} (Messengers bearing good tidings and warning, so that mankind might have no argument against God after the messengers) [Q 4:165]. The third is His saying, the Exalted: {«ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله، لقالوا: ربنا لو لا أرسلت إلينا رسولا، فنتبع آياتك من قبل أن نذل ونخزى»} (And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said: 'Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger, so that we might have followed Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?') [Q 20:134]. The fourth is His saying, the Exalted: {«أولم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر، وجاءكم النذير»} (Did We not give you lives long enough for whoever would remember to remember therein, and the warner came to you?) [Q 35:37]. And it is known that the meaning of this is: "We granted you respite and removed your excuse, so that no excuse or argument against Us would remain for you." The fifth is His saying, the Exalted: {«يوم تأتي كل نفس تجادل عن نفسها»} (The Day when every soul will come disputing on its own behalf) [Q 16:111]. And it is known that that disputation is only with one who calls it to account and is of its kind — and that is none other than God, the Exalted. Thus it necessarily follows that the servant's disputation is with God. The sixth is His saying, the Exalted, relating the words of the disbelievers: {«رب لم حشرتني أعمى. وقد كنت بصيرا»} (My Lord, why have You raised me blind, though I was seeing?) [Q 20:125]. Then He did not say in reply: {«لا يسئل عما يفعل»} (He is not questioned about what He does), but rather said: {«كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى»} (Thus did Our verses come to you, and you forgot them; and thus today you are forgotten) [Q 20:126]. The seventh is His saying: {«وأنفقوا من ما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت، فيقول: رب لو لا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب: فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين»} (And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you, and he says: 'My Lord, if only You would defer me to a near term, so that I might give charity and be among the righteous!') [Q 63:10].

chapters.title_en: The Refutation of the Mu'tazilite Arguments from the Qur'an on Divine Decree — Sections on the Excuse of the Unbelievers and the Command to Seek Aid
chapters.arabic_text:
فهذه الآيات دالة على أن الكفار يجعلون  عدم بعثة الأنبياء ، وعدم الإمهال عذرا لهم في ترك الإيمان. والله يقول : إني أزلت هذا العذر لئلا يبقى سؤالهم متوجها علي. فإذا كان هذا القدر من العذر ، وهو عدم بعثة الأنبياء عليهم السلام يقبله الله تعالى من الكفار فلأن لا يكون العبد ممنوعا عن الإيمان من الوجوه الاثني عشر التي ذكرناها ، لئلا يكون عذرا له في عدم الإيمان : كان أولى. بل نقول : هذا العذر أولى بالقبول. وذلك لأن الله تعالى لو بعث الرسل ، ولم يخلق الإيمان البتة لم يؤمن العبد البتة. ولو خلق الإيمان ، ولم يبعث الرسل ، لآمن لا محالة. فكيف يجوز أن يزيل الله عذرا ، لا تأثير له البتة ولا يزيل ما هو المؤثر الأصلي؟ فإن هذا يكون كالمناقض. وأما قوله تعالى : ( @QUR@04 لا يسئل عما يفعل ) فقالوا : المراد منه : لما ثبت بالدلائل أنه تعالى لا يفعل إلا ما هو حكمة وصواب ، لم يكن في السؤال عن كل واحد من التصور مزيد فائدة. بل العلم حاصل بأن أي شيء يفعله الله فهو حكمة وصواب. وليس المراد بأنه تعالى بلغ في الظلم مبلغا لا يسأل عن فعله خوفا من شره كالفراعنة والجبابرة ، والذين يظلمون ولا يسألون

عن فعلهم ، خوفا من شرهم.

فهذا تمام تقرير كلام القوم في هذا الباب.

والجواب : إن هذه الآيات دالة على أنه لا مانع للقوم من الإيمان. وقد دلنا بالوجوه الاثني عشر على قيام الموانع. ولا بد من التوفيق ، فتحمل هذه الآيات على عدم الموانع الظاهرة ، وتحمل الدلائل العقلية على قيام الموانع العقلية. عملا بالدليلين بقدر الإمكان.

والله أعلم

||| * النوع الرابع

||| * من وجوه استدلالات المعتزلة بالقرآن

الآيات التي أمر الله عباده فيها بأن يستعينوا بالله ، وبأن يعين بعضهم بعضا.

أما الاستعانة بالله : فكقوله تعالى : ( @QUR@02 إياك نستعين ) ( @QUR@05 فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم ) (1) ( @QUR@07 وقل رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين ) (2) ( @QUR@02 استعينوا بالله ) (3) وتقديره : إن الاستعانة إنما تعقل في حق من يقدر على الفعل ، لكنه لا يقدر على إتمامه وإكماله إلا بإعانة المعين. فلو لم يكن العبد قادرا على التكوين  والتحصيل كانت إعانته ممتنعة ، فكان أمره بالاستعانة عبثا. وأما الأمر بإعانة بعضهم بعضا. فكقوله تعالى : ( @QUR@09 وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ، ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان ) (4) ومن لم يقدر على الفعل أصلا فكيف يمكنه إعانة غيره على الفعل؟.

والجواب : مذهبنا : أن الملزوم للفعل هو مجموع القدرة والداعي. وذلك مشروط بإزالة الموانع. فإعانة الله لعبده. هو أن يزيل الموانع عن كون ذلك المجموع مستلزما لذلك الأثر.

وأما إعانة بعضهم بعضا : فهو أنه من الجائز أن لا تكون قدرة الإنسان الواحد وداعيته كافية في استلزام ذلك الفعل. بل لا بد فيه من قدر أناس كثيرين ومن دواعيهم ، حتى يترتب على مجموع تلك القدر وتلك الدواعي ، حصول ذلك الأثر. فزال الإشكال.

||| * النوع الخامس
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ذ-ر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes a genuine impediment or justification that absolves one from blame; an excuse (ʿudhr) is that which removes culpability.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, ʿudhr pertains to the removal of divine accountability when an agent lacks the capacity or means to act — a concept central to the debate on human agency (istitāʿah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for a valid excuse; metaphorically (majāz) when the excuse is merely apparent or superficial, as in the case of the unbelievers' pretext.
- Root: م-ن-ع (m-n-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To prevent, hinder, or obstruct; a barrier (māniʿ) that blocks an action from occurring.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, māniʿ refers to the impediments that prevent the conjunction of power (qudrah) and motive (dāʿī) from producing the act — a technical term in al-Rāzī's theory of action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical obstruction; metaphorical for intellectual or theological barriers, such as the twelve impediments al-Rāzī enumerates.
- Root: ع-و-ن (ʿ-w-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Assistance, aid, or support in accomplishing a task; the act of helping another to achieve an end.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine aid (iʿānah) is God's facilitation of an act by removing obstacles, not by creating the act itself — a key distinction in the Ashʿarite framework.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for mutual cooperation among humans; metaphorical for divine assistance, which is not a transfer of power but an enabling condition.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Priority (Qāʿidat al-Taqdīm wa'l-Taʾkhīr) — In the verse {«لا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ»}, the negation of questioning is parsed as a general statement (ʿāmm) whose scope is restricted by contextual evidence (qarīnah), requiring the interpreter to distinguish between the literal sense and the intended theological meaning.
chapters.translation:
I say: These verses indicate that the unbelievers take the non-sending of the prophets and the lack of respite as an excuse for their abandonment of faith. And God says: I have removed this excuse so that their questioning may no longer remain directed against Me. Now, if this measure of excuse — namely, the non-sending of the prophets, peace be upon them — is accepted by God, the Exalted, from the unbelievers, then it is all the more fitting that the servant not be prevented from faith by the twelve aspects which we have mentioned, so that it may not serve as an excuse for him in his lack of faith. Rather, we say: This excuse is more deserving of acceptance. That is because if God, the Exalted, had sent the messengers but had not created faith at all, the servant would never have believed. And if He had created faith but had not sent the messengers, he would inevitably have believed. So how is it permissible that God removes an excuse that has no effect whatsoever, yet does not remove that which is the true effective cause? For this would be like a contradiction.

As for His saying, the Exalted: {«لا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ»} (He is not questioned about what He does) (Qur'an 21:23), they said: The intended meaning is that since it is established by proofs that He, the Exalted, does not do anything except what is wisdom and correctness, there is no added benefit in questioning each particular act. Rather, knowledge is already attained that whatever God does is wisdom and correctness. And the intended meaning is not that He, the Exalted, has reached such a degree of injustice that He is not questioned about His act out of fear of His evil, like the Pharaohs and tyrants who oppress and are not questioned about their deeds, out of fear of their evil.

This completes the exposition of the people's (the Mu'tazilites') discourse on this topic.

And the answer: These verses indicate that there is no apparent obstacle preventing the people from faith. Yet we have demonstrated through the twelve aspects the existence of impediments. Reconciliation is necessary, so these verses are interpreted as referring to the absence of apparent impediments, while the rational proofs are interpreted as establishing the existence of intellectual impediments — acting upon both evidences to the extent possible.

And God knows best.

||| * The Fourth Type

||| * Of the Mu'tazilites' Modes of Argumentation from the Qur'an

The verses in which God, the Exalted, commands His servants to seek aid from God, and to aid one another.

As for seeking aid from God: Such as His saying, the Exalted: {«إِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ»} (You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help) (Qur'an 1:5), and {«فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ»} (So seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan) (Qur'an 16:98), and {«وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ»} (And say: My Lord, I seek refuge with You from the whisperings of the devils) (Qur'an 23:97), and {«اسْتَعِينُوا بِاللَّهِ»} (Seek help from Allah) (Qur'an 2:45). Its implication is: Seeking aid is only intelligible on the part of one who is capable of the act, but who cannot complete and perfect it except through the assistance of an aider. So if the servant were not capable of origination (takwīn) and acquisition (taḥṣīl), then aiding him would be impossible, and thus commanding him to seek aid would be futile.

As for the command to aid one another: Such as His saying, the Exalted: {«وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَىٰ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ»} (And cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression) (Qur'an 5:2). And whoever is not capable of the act at all — how could he possibly aid another in the act?

And the answer: Our doctrine is that that which entails the act is the totality of power (qudrah) and motive (dāʿī), and this is conditioned upon the removal of impediments. So God's aid to His servant is that He removes the impediments from that totality being entailing of that effect.

As for their aiding one another: It is that it is possible that the power of a single person and his motive are not sufficient for entailing that act. Rather, the powers of many people and their motives are necessary, so that upon the totality of those powers and those motives, the occurrence of that effect may follow. Thus the difficulty is removed.

||| * The Fifth Type

chapters.title_en: On the Qur'anic Arguments of the Determinists (Al-Mujbirah) Concerning the Impossibility of Burdening Beyond Capacity, and the Sixth Class of Their Proofs
chapters.arabic_text:
||| * من استدلالات القوم بالقرآن

وهو جميع الأدلة الدالة على أنه تعالى لم يكلف فوق الوسع والطاقة (1). قالوا : لو لم يكن العبد موجدا لأفعال نفسه ، لكان تكليفه بالفعل تكليفا بما لا يطاق ، وهذا باطل ، فذاك باطل. بيان الملازمة: إنه إذا كان فعل العبد واقعا بتكوين الله. فإن خلق ذلك الفعل لم يقدر على تحصيله لأن تحصيل الحاصل محال ، وإن لم يخلقه لم يقدر العبد أيضا على تحصيله. لأن قدرته غير

الأول : يجوز تكليف ما لا يطاق أو التكليف بالمحال لذاته أو لغيره وهو قول الأشعرية واضطربت الرواية عن الأشعري في وقوع ذلك وقال الجويني : «هذا سوء معرفة بمذهب الرجل فإن مقتضى مذهبه أن التكاليف كلها واقعة على خلاف الاستطاعة» (البرهان 1 / 103).

الثاني : يجوز التكليف بالمحال إلا أنه غير واقع شرعا. وبه قال الإمام القرافي في شرح تنقيح الفصول (ص 143).

الثالث : يجوز التكليف بالمحال لغيره ولا يجوز التكليف بالمحال لذاته. وهو قول معتزلة بغداد والآمدي والغزالي (قال الآمدي : وإليه ميل الغزالي رحمه الله تعالى) وابن القشيري وأبي بكر الصيرفي.

الرابع : لا يجوز التكليف بالمحال الذي ليس ممتنعا لتعلق العلم بعدم وقوعه. وبه قال أكثر المعتزلة وأبو حامد الأسفراييني والغزالي وابن دقيق العيد والحنفية.

الخامس : ميز إمام الحرمين بين الطلب والورود فمنع كون المحال مطلوبا  وأجاز ورود صيغة الطلب بالتكليف بالمحال. قال : إن أريد بالتكليف طلب الفعل فهو فيما لا يطاق محال من العالم باستحالة وقوع المطلوب. وإن أريد به ورود الصيغة وليس المراد به طلبا كقوله سبحانه ( كونوا قردة خاسئين ) فهذا غير ممتنع» (البرهان 1 / 104).

راجع المسألة في كتب الأصول أصول الدين وأصول الفقه : مجرد مقالات الأشعري (110 124)؛ أصول الدين للبغدادي (212 213)؛ المواقف للإيجي (330 331)، البرهان للجويني (1 / 101 105)؛ الإرشاد للجويني (203 204)؛ المحصول للرازي 1 / 302 316 ؛ التحصيل من المحصول للأرموي 1 / 316 321)؛ شرح تنقيح الفصول للقرافي (ص 143)؛ معالم أصول الدين للرازي (ص 91). محصل أفكار المتقدمين والمتأخرين للرازي (153)؛ المطالب العالية له أيضا (3 / 305 315). المعتمد في أصول الدين لأبي يعلى (146 147)؛ الابهاج شرح المنهاج للسبكي (1 / 171 176)؛ الإحكام في أصول الأحكام للآمدي (1 / 179 191)؛ نهاية السئول للإسنوي (1 / 345 352)؛ حاشية البناني (1 / 206 210) ؛ المعتمد لأبي الحسن البصري (1 / 164 165)؛ أصول السرخسي (1 / 65 73)؛ كشف الأسرار شرح أصول البزدوي للبخاري (1 / 191)؛ تيسر التحرير لمحمد آمين (2 / 137 141)؛ التقرير والتحبير لابن أمير الحاج (2 / 82 87)؛ التلويح على التوضيح لصدر الشريعة (1 / 197 201)؛ كشف الأسرار شرح المنار للنسفي (1 / 98 99)؛ فواتح الرحموت شرح مسلم الثبوت (1 / 123 128)؛ الموافقات للشاطبي (2 / 107 108)؛ منتهى ابن الحاجب (41). روضة الناظر لابن قدامة (52 54)؛ المسودة (52 53)؛ المدخل إلى مذهب الإمام أحمد لابن بدران (146) ؛ إرشاد الفحول للشوكاني (9 10).

صالحة للتحصيل فثبت : أن العبد لو لم يكن موجدا لأفعال نفسه ، لكان تكليفه تكليفا بما لا يطاق. وإنما قلنا : إن ذلك باطل. لقوله تعالى : ( @QUR@06 لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها ) (1) ولقوله تعالى : ( @QUR@04 ولا يريد بكم العسر ) (2) ومعلوم : أن تكليف ما لا يطاق أعظم أنواع العسر ولقوله: ( @QUR@07 وما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج ) (3) ولا حرج فوق أن يكون الإنسان مكلفا بما لا طاقة له به. والجواب : إنا بينا أن تكليف ما لا يطاق لازم على المعتزلة من الوجوه الاثني عشر التي ذكرناها وقررناها. فلا فائدة في الإعادة. وإذا كان كذلك فتحمل هذه الآيات على عدم  الظاهرية.

||| * النوع السادس

||| * من وجوه القوم

أن قالوا : لو كان الله تعالى موجدا للكفر والمعاصي ، لكان مريدا لها. وهذا باطل فذاك باطل. بيان الملازمة : إن المجبرة ساعدوا على أنه تعالى لو كان خالقا لأعمال العباد ، لكن مريدا لها. وبيان هذه المساعدة من وجهين :

الأول : إنهم في مسألة إرادة الكائنات. قالوا : لما ثبت أن الله خلق أعمال العباد ، وجب أن يكون مريدا لها.

والثاني : أنهم قالوا إنه تعالى لما خصص بعض أفعاله ، بإحداثه في وقت معين ، ومحل معين ، مع جواز أن يخلقه في وقت آخر ، وفي محل آخر ، وجب أن يكون ذلك التخصيص لأجل الإرادة. فثبت : أنه تعالى لو كان موجدا لأفعال العباد ، لكان مريدا لها وبيان أنه تعالى غير مريد لها : قوله تعالى : ( @QUR@07 كل ذلك كان سيئه عند ربك مكروها ) (1) والمكروه لا يكون مرادا لامتناع الجمع بين الضدين. وتمام الكلام في هذا المقام ، والاستدلال بجميع الآيات التي يتمسكون بها في أنه تعالى غير مريد للقبائح سيأتي الاستقصاء فيه في مسألة إرادة الكائنات إن شاء الله.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ل-ف (K-L-F)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To burden, charge, or impose a task upon someone; the root denotes the imposition of a weighty obligation (taklīf) that entails effort and strain upon the one charged.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, taklīf signifies the divine imposition of a command or prohibition upon the morally responsible agent (mukallaf), which presupposes the agent's capacity (istitāʿah) to comply or disobey.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense (ḥaqīqah) is the imposition of a burden; the metaphorical sense (majāz) extends to any divine address that obligates the servant, even if the act is impossible (muḥāl), as in the command to the Jews to become apes.
- Root: و-س-ع (W-S-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Capacity, amplitude, or breadth; the root signifies that which is within one's power or scope to perform without undue hardship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'anic context {«لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا»}, it denotes the limit of human capability that God takes into account in His legislation, excluding what lies beyond the agent's natural power.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is physical or material breadth; the metaphorical sense is the moral and legal capacity that renders an obligation just and feasible.
- Root: ك-ر-ه (K-R-H)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To dislike, abhor, or detest; the root conveys a strong aversion of the heart toward something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In divine attributes, karāhah (dislike) is used to negate any attribution of volition (irādah) toward evil or abominable acts (qabāʾiḥ), for God's will is exclusively directed toward good.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is the emotional state of aversion; the metaphorical sense in theological discourse denotes the ontological impossibility of God willing what He declares detestable, given the impossibility of conjoining opposites.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Implication (Qānūn al-Luzūm) — In the structure "لو لم يكن... لكان... وبيان الملازمة," the conditional sentence establishes a necessary entailment (mulāzamah) between the antecedent and consequent, requiring the interlocutor to either affirm the consequent or reject the antecedent; the parsing follows the pattern of a hypothetical syllogism where the proof of the entailment is the crux of the argument.
chapters.translation:
I say: This is the totality of the proofs indicating that He, exalted be He, has not burdened anyone beyond capacity and power (ṭāqah). They said: If the servant were not the originator (mūjid) of his own acts, then his being burdened with the act would be a burdening with that which cannot be endured (mā lā yuṭāq), and this is false; therefore, that [premise] is false. The demonstration of the entailment (mulāzamah) is that if the servant's act occurs by God's bringing-into-being (takwīn), then either He created that act — in which case the servant has no power to procure it, for procuring what already exists (taḥṣīl al-ḥāṣil) is impossible — or He did not create it, in which case the servant likewise has no power to procure it, because his power is not fit for acquisition (taḥṣīl). Thus it is established that if the servant were not the originator of his own acts, his being burdened would be a burdening with what cannot be endured. And we say that this is false, due to His saying, exalted be He: {«لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا»} (God does not burden any soul beyond its capacity), and His saying: {«وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ»} (And He does not desire hardship for you), and it is known that burdening with what cannot be endured is the greatest kind of hardship; and His saying: {«وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ»} (And He has placed no constraint upon you in religion), and there is no constraint greater than a human being being burdened with what he has no power to perform.

The answer: We have already demonstrated that burdening with what cannot be endured is entailed upon the Muʿtazilah from the twelve aspects which we have mentioned and established. There is no benefit in repetition. And since this is so, these verses are to be interpreted as not carrying their apparent meaning (ẓāhir).

||| * The Sixth Class

||| * Of Their Proofs

They said: If God, exalted be He, were the originator of unbelief (kufr) and acts of disobedience (maʿāṣī), then He would be willing (murīd) of them. And this is false; therefore, that [premise] is false. The demonstration of the entailment: The determinists (al-mujbirah) have conceded that if He, exalted be He, were the creator of the servants' acts, then He would be willing of them. The demonstration of this concession is from two aspects:

The first: In the question of the will concerning originated things (irādat al-kāʾināt), they said: Since it is established that God created the servants' acts, it necessarily follows that He is willing of them.

The second: They said that since He, exalted be He, specified some of His acts by bringing them into existence at a particular time and in a particular locus, despite the possibility of creating them at another time and in another locus, that specification must be due to will (irādah). Thus it is established that if He, exalted be He, were the originator of the servants' acts, He would be willing of them. And the demonstration that He, exalted be He, is not willing of them is His saying, exalted be He: {«كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ كَانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهًا»} (All of that — its evil is detestable in the sight of your Lord). And the detestable (makrūh) cannot be willed (murād), because of the impossibility of conjoining two opposites. The complete discussion of this station, and the argumentation with all the verses they employ to prove that He, exalted be He, does not will abominable acts (qabāʾiḥ), will be exhaustively treated in the question of the will concerning originated things, God willing.

chapters.title_en: The Seventh and Eighth Categories of Arguments for the Determinists (Al-Mujbirah) — On Divine Recompense and Human Capability
chapters.arabic_text:
||| * النوع السابع للقوم

الآيات الدالة على أنه متى فعل العبد فعلا ، فإنه تعالى يجازيه بفعل آخر.

وتقديره : أن نقول : القرآن يدل على أن العبد قد يفعل أمورا. متى فعلها ، فإنه تعالى يجازيه عليها بأفعال أخرى. ومتى كان الأمر كذلك ، وجب أن تكون تلك الأفعال واقعة بتكوين العبد ، لا بتكوين الله تعالى. بيان المقدمة الأولى : إن الآيات : ( @QUR@04 جزاء بما كانوا يعملون ) (1) ( @QUR@04 جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون ) (2) ( @QUR@09 ليجزي الذين أساؤا بما عملوا ، ويجزي الذين أحسنوا بالحسنى ) (3) ( @QUR@012 يا أيها الذين كفروا لا تعتذروا اليوم. إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون ) (4) ( @QUR@04 ذلك بما قدمت يداك ) (5) ( @QUR@06 اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت ) (6) ( @QUR@07 فأخذتهم صاعقة العذاب الهون بما كانوا يكسبون ) (7) هذه الآيات وأمثالها دالة على أن العبد إذا أتى بهذه الأفعال فإنه تعالى يجازيه عليها بأفعال أخرى. وبيان المقدمة الثانية. وهي قولنا : إن ذلك يقتضي أن لا يكون فعل العبد فعلا لله تعالى. فتقديره من وجهين :

الأول : إنه لو كان الشرط فعلا لله  تعالى ، كما أن الجزاء فعله ، لصار العبد من هذا الشرط والجزاء خارجا من البين ، ويصير التقدير كأنه تعالى يقول : إني متى فعلت الفعل الفلاني فإني أفعل بعده فعلا آخر. إلا أن التغاير بين هذا الكلام وبين قوله أيها العبد إن أطعتني أثبتك ، وإن عصيتني عاقبتك : معلوم بالضرورة.

الثاني : إنه تعالى إنما رتب هذه الأجزية على أفعال العباد ترغيبا لهم في الطاعات ومنعا لهم عن المحظورات. وهذا إنما يفيد إذا كانوا قادرين على الفعل والترك ، متمكنين من كل واحد منهما على البذل. وقد بينا : أنه لو كان موجد أفعال العباد هو الله تعالى لما بقيت هذه القدرة

وحينئذ يصير هذا الترغيب والترهيب عبثا بالكلية. ومما يؤكد ذلك قوله تعالى : ( @QUR@021 وقالوا : اتخذ الرحمن ولدا. لقد جئتم شيئا إدا. تكاد السماوات يتفطرن منه وتنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا : أن دعوا للرحمن ولدا ) (1) واستدلال به من وجهين :

الأول : إن ذلك القول لو كان مخلوقا لله تعالى لصار الكلام ركيكا لأنه يصير تقدير الكلام : تكاد السموات أجعلها منفطرة والأرضين أجعلها منشقة بما خلقت في العبد هذا الكلام ، وأردته وقضيت به. ومعلوم : أن ذلك في غاية الركاكة. وأيضا : فقوله : ( @QUR@04 لقد جئتم شيئا إدا ). نص في أن العبد هو الذي جاء بذلك الفعل.

الثاني : إن الواحد منا إذا أنكر على غيره فعلا ، ثم أتى بمثله عد سفيها. قال تعالى : ( @QUR@05 أتأمرون الناس بالبر ، وتنسون أنفسكم ) (2)؟ فلما عاب عليهم قولهم إن ولدا للرحمن فالذي خلق ذلك القول فيهم يكون العبث عليه ألزم. لو أن قائلا قال : تأملوا قبح قولهم إن للرحمن ولدا ، ومن قبحه انفطرت السموات وانشقت الأرض فانهدت الجبال ثم مع ذلك فإني أنا الذي فعلت ذلك ، وخلقته فيهم وقضيته عليهم وأردته منهم. لقال الناس : ما أشد حماقة هذا القائل ، وما أقبح صنعه. وإذا كان الأمر كذلك ، فكيف يليق هذا برب العالمين؟.

والجواب : إن عندنا مجموع القدرة والداعي ، موجب للفعل ، وعلى هذا التقدير فهذه الإلزامات ساقطة عنا. وأيضا : فالوجوه الاثني عشر المذكورة دالة على وقوع تكليف ما لا  يطاق ، وكل ذلك يبطل هذه الكلمات.

والله أعلم

||| * النوع الثامن للقوم

الآيات الدالة على كون العبد متمكنا من الإيمان والكفر ، قادرا على الخير والشر.

قال تعالى : ( @QUR@06 فمن شاء فليؤمن ، ومن شاء فليكفر ) (1) وقال : ( @QUR@05 لمن شاء منكم أن يستقيم ) (2) وقال : ( @QUR@07 إنا هديناه السبيل ، إما شاكرا وإما كفورا ) (3) وقال : ( @QUR@02 وهديناه النجدين ) (4) أي طريقي الخير والشر. وقال : ( @QUR@06 ونفس وما سواها. فألهمها فجورها وتقواها ) (5) والجواب : إنا ذكرنا هذه الآيات دليلا لنا. لأنها تقتضي تعليل الفعل. بالمشيئة. ومشيئة العبد معلقة بمشيئة الله تعالى ، فيكون فعل العبد معلقا بمشيئة الله تعالى. من هذا الوجه.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-ز-ى (j-z-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "recompense" or "requital" — the giving of a return (jazā') proportionate to an act, whether good or evil.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, jazā' denotes God's equitable retribution or reward, which presupposes a prior act attributable to a moral agent; it is a correlate (muqābalah) of the deed.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage requires the act and its recompense to belong to the same order of agency; metaphorical (majāz) usage would sever this causal-moral link, rendering the verse rhetorically incoherent.
- Root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To earn" or "acquire" — an act whereby one draws a consequence upon oneself.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Kasb in Kalām denotes the human act as a locus of moral responsibility, distinct from divine creation (khalq); it implies voluntary acquisition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The verse "بما كانوا يكسبون" (for what they used to earn) is literal in attributing the earning to the servant, not to God.
- Root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Will" or "volition" — the inclination of the soul toward an action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Mashī'ah in the Qur'an is hierarchically ordered: the servant's will is subordinate to the divine will, yet the verse "فمن شاء فليؤمن" (so whoever wills, let him believe) grants the servant a real volitional capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The imperative "فليؤمن" (let him believe) is a command addressed to one capable of compliance, indicating literal possibility (imkān), not mere metaphor.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional-Protasis Construction (al-sharṭ wa'l-jazā') — In Arabic syntax, the protasis (sharṭ) and apodosis (jazā') are grammatically linked such that the condition's fulfillment is the cause of the result; if both are attributed to the same agent (God), the conditional structure collapses into a tautology, which Sībawayh would deem a violation of meaningful discourse (khiṭāb mufīd).
chapters.translation:
||| * The Seventh Category for the Determinists

The verses indicating that when the servant performs an act, God — exalted is He — recompenses him with another act.

Its formulation is that we say: The Qur'an indicates that the servant may perform certain things. When he performs them, God — exalted is He — recompenses him for them with other acts. And when the matter is thus, those [recompensing] acts must be brought into existence by the servant's own origination (takwīn), not by God's origination. The demonstration of the first premise: The verses — {«جزاء بما كانوا يعملون»} (a recompense for what they used to do) (Q 46:14), {«جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون»} (a recompense for what they used to earn) (Q 34:37), {«ليجزي الذين أساؤا بما عملوا، ويجزي الذين أحسنوا بالحسنى»} (that He may recompense those who did evil for what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best) (Q 53:31), {«يا أيها الذين كفروا لا تعتذروا اليوم. إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون»} (O you who disbelieve, do not excuse yourselves today. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do) (Q 66:7), {«ذلك بما قدمت يداك»} (That is for what your hands have sent forth) (Q 22:10), {«اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت»} (Today every soul is recompensed for what it has earned) (Q 40:17), {«فأخذتهم صاعقة العذاب الهون بما كانوا يكسبون»} (So the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn) (Q 41:17) — these verses and their like indicate that when the servant performs these acts, God — exalted is He — recompenses him for them with other acts.

And the demonstration of the second premise — namely, our statement that this entails that the servant's act not be an act of God — exalted is He — is formulated from two angles:

The first: If the condition [i.e., the servant's act] were an act of God — exalted is He — just as the recompense is His act, then the servant would drop out of the picture entirely between this condition and this recompense, and the formulation would become as though God — exalted is He — says: "When I perform such-and-such an act, I perform after it another act." Yet the difference between this speech and His saying — O servant, if you obey Me, I reward you, and if you disobey Me, I punish you — is known by necessity.

The second: God — exalted is He — only attached these recompenses to the acts of the servants as an inducement (targhīb) for them toward acts of obedience and a deterrent (tarhīb) against forbidden things. This is only beneficial if they are capable of acting and refraining, empowered over each of the two with full capacity. And we have already demonstrated: if the originator of the servants' acts were God — exalted is He — this capability would not remain. And in that case, this inducement and deterrence would become utterly futile (ʿabath).

What reinforces this is His saying — exalted is He: {«وقالوا: اتخذ الرحمن ولدا. لقد جئتم شيئا إدا. تكاد السماوات يتفطرن منه وتنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا: أن دعوا للرحمن ولدا»} (And they say: The Most Merciful has taken a son. You have come with something monstrous. The heavens almost burst apart from it, and the earth splits, and the mountains collapse in ruin — that they attribute a son to the Most Merciful) (Q 19:88-91). And the inference from it is from two angles:

The first: If that statement were created by God — exalted is He — the speech would become feeble (rakīk), because the formulation of the speech would become: "The heavens — I make them nearly bursting apart, and the earths — I make them splitting, because of what I created in the servant of this statement, and willed it, and decreed it." And it is known that this is utterly feeble. Also, His saying: {«لقد جئتم شيئا إدا»} (You have come with something monstrous) is an explicit text (naṣṣ) that the servant is the one who came with that act.

The second: When one of us reproaches another for an act, then commits the like of it, he is deemed foolish. God — exalted is He — said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر، وتنسون أنفسكم»} (Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?) (Q 2:44). So since He censured them for their statement that the Most Merciful has a son, then the One who created that statement in them would be even more liable to the charge of futility. If a speaker were to say: "Reflect upon the ugliness of their statement that the Most Merciful has a son — and from its ugliness the heavens burst, the earth split, and the mountains collapsed — yet despite that, I am the one who did that, created it in them, decreed it upon them, and willed it from them" — people would say: "How severe is this speaker's foolishness, and how ugly his deed!" And when the matter is thus, how could this befit the Lord of the Worlds?

The answer: For us, the conjunction of capability (qudrah) and motive (dāʿī) necessitates the act; and on this formulation, these objections fall away from us. Also, the twelve aforementioned arguments indicate the occurrence of the imposition of what cannot be borne (taklīf mā lā yuṭāq), and all of that invalidates these statements.

And God knows best.

||| * The Eighth Category for the Determinists

The verses indicating that the servant is empowered over faith and disbelief, capable of good and evil.

God — exalted is He — said: {«فمن شاء فليؤمن، ومن شاء فليكفر»} (So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve) (Q 18:29). And He said: {«لمن شاء منكم أن يستقيم»} (For whoever among you wills to be upright) (Q 81:28). And He said: {«إنا هديناه السبيل، إما شاكرا وإما كفورا»} (Indeed, We guided him to the path — either grateful or ungrateful) (Q 76:3). And He said: {«وهديناه النجدين»} (And We guided him to the two highways) (Q 90:10) — that is, the two paths of good and evil. And He said: {«ونفس وما سواها. فألهمها فجورها وتقواها»} (And a soul and what proportioned it. Then He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness) (Q 91:7-8).

The answer: We have already cited these verses as an argument for ourselves, because they entail the causation of the act by the will (mashī'ah). And the servant's will is suspended upon the will of God — exalted is He — so the servant's act is suspended upon the will of God — exalted is He — from this angle.
